explainedBy: The leverage-points passage opens on the giant humming factory the hosts ask us to picture.

storyboard.claim: Meadows' leverage points, pictured as a massive steampunk factory.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A factory with smoking chimneys fills the frame.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers 'where do we push?' by introducing the factory metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the stage (the machine) the next beats keep.

explainedBy: The same factory stays; the frantic politician now stands in front of it.

storyboard.claim: The machine is the size of a building; a frantic politician stands before it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The sweating politician appears in front of the factory.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same factory; the politician enters.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces who is working the machine.

explainedBy: The politician reaches for and twists a tiny dial labeled tax rate.

storyboard.claim: He furiously twists a tiny dial labeled tax rate.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Politician reaching to a control-panel dial.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The factory gives way to the small dial he is fixated on.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the action: twisting a small dial.

explainedBy: The same politician keeps twisting the same dial, now sweating, up 1% and down 2%.

storyboard.claim: He tweaks it up 1%, down 2%, hoping to find the magic number.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same dial, same reaching politician; his face turns more anxious.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept stage; face escalates, callout gives the tweaks.
storyboard.addedInformation: The specific tiny adjustments he tries.

explainedBy: Meanwhile a giant iron lever sits unused in the corner, nobody at it.

storyboard.claim: Ignored in the corner, covered in dust, is a giant iron lever.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The giant iron lever alone in the frame, no one touching it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cuts from the busy dial to the untouched lever.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrast: small dial worked, big lever ignored.

explainedBy: The same untouched lever gets its label: paradigm.

storyboard.claim: The lever is labeled paradigm; Meadows ranked leverage points.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same lever, now named.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept lever; adds its label.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names what the big lever stands for.

explainedBy: Meadows' list runs from 12 (weakest) to 1 (most powerful), and people instinctively grab the weakest end.

storyboard.claim: Leverage points are ranked 12 weakest to 1 most powerful; humans grab the weakest.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A spectrum from 12 weakest to 1 most powerful, the marker at the weak end.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the dial-vs-lever image into Meadows' ranked list.
storyboard.addedInformation: The 12-to-1 scale and where we instinctively push.

explainedBy: Back at the machine: the politician reaches for the dial, as we all grab the parameters.

storyboard.claim: We grab the dials: numbers, parameters, subsidies.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Politician reaching for the control dial again.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the dial after the ranking.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the 'weakest' end to the dial image.

explainedBy: The same politician at the same dial argues heatedly over 4% versus 4.5%.

storyboard.claim: We spend election cycles and billions arguing over 4% or 4.5% interest rates or tax brackets.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same dial; the politician now angrily points, arguing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept stage; reaching becomes arguing.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tiny numbers fought over.

explainedBy: The speed-limit argument: a road whose number is 55 or 65, a tangible, easy number.

storyboard.claim: Speed limit 55 or 65, because numbers are tangible and easy to quantify.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A road, with the two speed numbers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from tax numbers to the speed-limit number.
storyboard.addedInformation: Third example of a number we argue over.

explainedBy: Cause -> effect: changing a physical number leads to the system routing around it.

storyboard.claim: Changing a number almost never changes a complex system's behavior; it routes around it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow: Change a number -> System routes around.
storyboard.onScreenText: Change a number -> System routes around
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the general lesson of the examples.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mechanism of why tweaks fail.

explainedBy: Lower the speed limit without redesigning the road, and the everyman on that road just speeds again.

storyboard.claim: Lower the speed limit without changing road design and people speed again.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman moving down the same road, unbothered by the new limit.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concrete case of 'routes around it'.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the rig cannot draw a car speeding; walk on the highway stands in.

explainedBy: Donella points to the goal itself: lever number three is changing the system's goals.

storyboard.claim: The strong levers are 3, 2, 1; three is changing the goals of the system.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donella pointing at a target.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From weak levers to the strong ones at the top.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lever three named and shown as a goal.

explainedBy: Donella now points to the big iron lever: number two is changing the paradigm.

storyboard.claim: Two is changing the paradigm; one is transcending paradigms altogether.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same Donella; the target is replaced by the giant paradigm lever.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept speaker; the object she points at moves up the list.
storyboard.addedInformation: Connects lever two to the lever from the factory.

explainedBy: Meadows beside the paradigm lever: no paradigm is absolute truth.
noVisual: Transcending paradigms has no object in the vocabulary; text carries it with the same speaker.

storyboard.claim: Number one is realizing no paradigm is absolute truth; but it is not simple to do.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Meadows beside the paradigm lever: no paradigm is absolute truth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept speaker; reaches the top of the list. (fix round 2)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the idea is carried by the text.

explainedBy: The politician reaches toward the paradigm lever and recoils: throwing it is excruciating, unlike the dial.

storyboard.claim: Throwing the paradigm lever is excruciating; changing numbers is easy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Politician reaching fearfully toward the big lever.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back at the machine: the politician faces the lever he ignored.
storyboard.addedInformation: Why he twists the dial instead.

explainedBy: Changing a number is easy: the politician just takes the bill.

storyboard.claim: Changing numbers is passing a bill or memo; a paradigm needs millions to admit their worldview may be wrong.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Changing a number is easy: the politician takes the bill beside the little dial.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrast: easy paper fix vs the hard lever. (fix round 2)
storyboard.addedInformation: The easy action made physical.

explainedBy: The everyman slumps holding the story he built his identity around, facing that it might be flawed.

storyboard.claim: People must admit the story they built their identity and self-worth around might be flawed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman slumped, holding a book (his life story).
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the politician's easy fix to the ordinary person's hard admission.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the book stands for 'the story they built'.

explainedBy: The man at the machine angrily defends the paradigm lever: systems fight back against change.

storyboard.claim: People hate it; systems fiercely protect their paradigms, up to violence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Angry politician beside the paradigm lever, warding off change.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From personal pain to the system's defense.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: violence is not drawn; anger carries the resistance.

explainedBy: Donella points at the growing snowball and rejects endless exponential growth as the economy's goal.

storyboard.claim: Tell a nation its economy's goal should be sustainable balance, not endless exponential growth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Snowball rolling and growing; 'endless exponential growth' struck out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: An example of attacking a core paradigm.
storyboard.addedInformation: The paradigm being challenged, shown as runaway growth.

callout.text: The system will attack you back

explainedBy: The politician angrily turns on Donella, who challenged the paradigm: the system attacks back.

storyboard.claim: Attack the core paradigm and the system attacks you back; new laws, CEOs or diets change nothing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Angry politician pointing at Donella.
storyboard.onScreenText: The system will attack you back
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The challenge of the last beat meets resistance.
storyboard.addedInformation: Who pushes back against whom.

explainedBy: Five years on nothing changed: the everyman slumps beside the dial he merely twisted.

storyboard.claim: Five years later nothing changed; you only twisted a dial.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman slumped next to the control dial.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Result of the reforms: no change.
storyboard.addedInformation: Links failed reforms back to the dial image.

explainedBy: Cause -> effect: the paradigm drives the structure, and the structure produces the behavior.

storyboard.claim: The behavior is in the structure, and that structure is driven by its paradigm.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow: Paradigm -> Structure -> Behavior.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sums up the leverage section.
storyboard.addedInformation: The causal order of the whole argument.

explainedBy: Recap of the examples, ending on the fisherman slumped by his trawler after the fisheries crashed.

storyboard.claim: We've built the bathtub, frozen with coffee, escalated in the back seat, crashed the fisheries.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sad fisherman beside the fishing trawler.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Recap before the pushback.
storyboard.addedInformation: Recalls one earlier case visually.

explainedBy: The host pushes back hard, pointing: isn't blaming the system a cowardly copout?

storyboard.claim: Isn't saying it's the system's fault just a cowardly copout?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host angrily pointing, challenging.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Breaks from recap into objection.
storyboard.addedInformation: The challenge to the book's premise.

explainedBy: The smirking CEO signs papers in front of a polluting factory: do we blame structure for corporate greed?

storyboard.claim: If we blame structure for the drug trade or corporate greed poisoning a river...
storyboard.concreteVisual: Smirking CEO with papers, a smoking factory.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Objection made concrete with an example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts a 'bad individual' on screen.

explainedBy: Back to the opening slinky: if it bounces no matter whose hand drops it, who is accountable?

storyboard.claim: Are we letting bad individuals off the hook? If the slinky bounces regardless of whose hand drops it, why hold anyone accountable?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A hand holding the bouncing slinky.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reuses the opening metaphor for the objection.
storyboard.addedInformation: The hand vs the spring: person vs structure.

explainedBy: The CEO smirks behind a mask: 'it's the system' as a pretty excuse for destructive behavior.

storyboard.claim: It sounds like an intellectual excuse for destructive behavior.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The CEO smirks behind a mask: 'it's the system' as a pretty excuse for destructive behavior.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the CEO the objection is about. (fix round 2)
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows who benefits from the excuse.

explainedBy: Donella answers: it is the most common pushback and a valid fear.
noVisual: Acknowledging an objection has no object; the speaker plus text carry it.

storyboard.claim: It is the most common pushback and a completely valid fear.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donella replying.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The answer begins.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: text-carried.

explainedBy: The everyman points away, shrugging off blame; the claim 'nothing is my fault' is struck out.

storyboard.claim: 'If everything is the system, nothing is my fault' misunderstands Meadows.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman smirking, pointing elsewhere; the phrase struck.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the misreading the host rejects.
storyboard.addedInformation: Blame-shifting shown, then rejected.

explainedBy: The same everyman now looks into a mirror: the system is not alien, it is us.

storyboard.claim: The system isn't an alien entity imposed on us. It is us.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same everyman, now holding a mirror, surprised.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept person; pointing away becomes facing himself.
storyboard.addedInformation: The turn from blaming others to seeing oneself in the system.

explainedBy: Bounded rationality: each person sees only the small part of the system under their own lens.
noVisual: The term itself has no object; the next beat shows it.

storyboard.claim: Meadows points out a concept called bounded rationality.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Bounded rationality: each person sees only the small part of the system under their own lens.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the tool that answers the objection. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: names the term.

explainedBy: The everyman looks through a magnifier at only a tiny part: rational within what he can see.

storyboard.claim: Everyone acts rationally within the tiny part of the system they can see.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman peering through a magnifying glass.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains bounded rationality as a narrow view.
storyboard.addedInformation: Narrow view made physical.

explainedBy: The drug trade, person by person: first the addict, in pain, seeking relief; the dealer beside him.

storyboard.claim: The addict wants relief from pain, rational for him; the dealer wants to feed his family.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worn-out man slumped in pain, the dealer next to him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts the drug-trade example.
storyboard.addedInformation: The first actor and his motive.

explainedBy: The dealer (zero jobs, feeding his family) stays; the officer, wanting order on her street, points at him.

storyboard.claim: The dealer feeds his family with zero jobs; the officer wants order and a promotion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same street; the officer enters pointing at the dealer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept dealer and street; the officer joins.
storyboard.addedInformation: The third actor and her motive; the relation between them.

explainedBy: All three now on the same street: each makes a rational choice from their own constraints.

storyboard.claim: Each makes a rational, maybe well-intentioned choice from their immediate constraints; but the subpurposes interact.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The dealer, the officer and the addict together.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept street; the addict rejoins so all three stand together.
storyboard.addedInformation: Groups the three separate rationalities.

explainedBy: Cause -> effect: their rational subpurposes add up to a violent drug war no one wants.

storyboard.claim: The subpurposes add up to a horrific, unending drug war that no one wants.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow: Rational subpurposes -> Unending drug war.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The result of the three choices.
storyboard.addedInformation: The emergent system behavior.

explainedBy: The officer peers through a magnifier at only her own small part, blind to the whole.

storyboard.claim: They aren't evil; they are blind to the whole, seeing only their own small loop.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Officer with a magnifier, the dealer beside her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the actors; the magnifier from 'the part they can see' returns.
storyboard.addedInformation: Narrow view, not evil intent.

explainedBy: Donella rejects the idea that this lets individuals off the hook.

storyboard.claim: This does not let individuals off the hook.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donella pointing; 'off the hook' struck out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the accountability objection.
storyboard.addedInformation: The answer: no, it does not excuse them.

explainedBy: The everyman reaches out beyond himself toward another person: taking responsibility by widening who he cares about.
noVisual: No icon reads as 'boundaries of caring'; a person reaching beyond himself is the clearest staging.

storyboard.claim: It places a heavier moral burden on us: individuals must expand their boundaries of caring.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman reaching out toward his partner.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From blind actors to the individual's responsibility.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: reaching outward stands for widening care.
